notes.title: Patch 1.0.5 - Controller support!
notes.content: [p]So this patch ended up being smaller than anticipated, because I finally got around to adding controller support! It took a lot more work than I thought it would, and some issues may remain which are pretty much unfixable, but it *should* be good enough for most people's purposes, and unfortunately, getting it up to the standards of everything else would likely take months, so it just kind of is what it is. Still, the game is fully playable with a joypad now. Just a few things to note:[/p][p]-The key rebind system does not support the joypad, I may change this if a lot of people feel they need it, although I can't promise that it will ever work perfectly, it's a bit finicky and is some causing some issues with it already.[/p][p]-On that note, if you wish to use the controller, [b]YOU WILL NEED TO NAVIGATE TO THE SAVE DIRECTORY[/b] (C:\\Users\\(user)\\AppData\\Roaming\\Godot\\app_userdata\\Shadowed- The Demon Castle of Ooe ) [b]AND DELETE keymaps.dat.[/b] The reason why I didn't do this automatically is because it would have reset everybody's keybinds, and I feel that controller users are probably in the minority here. Sorry about the inconvenience.[/p][h2]Gameplay:[/h2][p]-Balance changes coming soon![/p][h2]QOL:[/h2][p]-Added controller support![/p][p]-Added a "controller controls" help file. Unfortunately, this is the best I can do when it comes to teaching the player how to use the controller, adding functionality to hundreds of different buttons scattered everywhere to make them display controller commands would have taken multiple weeks.[/p][p]-Mouse support has been improved, mostly as a side-effect on the controller support. Right-clicking will now bring up the controller context menu, although there do remain a few things that you will have to do with keyboard in addition to mouse (namely magic/techniques/pausing since there are controller button binds for those).[/p][h2]Bugfixes:[/h2][p]-Fixed a bug where unequipping a talisman may have been causing problems.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.4 - Weekly
notes.content: [p]Another week mostly devoted to translation behind the scenes. But the vast bulk of my portion of the work is now done, so next week, I'll be able to do a lot more QOL and gameplay changes![/p][h2]Gameplay:[/h2][p]-The Poultice->Curing pill crafting recipe now has a 60% fail chance, to help balance out the cheap cost of taking poultices on character generation (didn't want to nerf the poultice option itself, wounds can be quite devastating early on).[/p][p]-Increased noise from the yell command.[/p][h2]QOL:[/h2][p]-Cleaned up a bunch of messages to only play when a monster is in sight (being stunned, etc).[/p][p]-The "highest class win" section in score now reads "highest ascension class win", as it was causing confusion.[/p][h2]Bugfixes:[/h2][p]-Fixed a bug where bear traps were inflicting the root status effect on the player but it did nothing(the root was supposed to be removed).[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where the main menu music would not play when exiting from game.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where stepping on a trap with extra move actions would softlock.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where monsters could not smell you through passageways.[/p][p]-Fixed(?) an issue where weapons could be spawned with negative quality.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.3 - PDF manual + The Usual
notes.content: [p]Another weekly patch again, once again there is little to note here. The translation is still going, although its a very long and tedious grind. In the meantime, lots of people have found a lot of bugs and issues, and I always appreciate the reports, even if it's a pain to see the bugs themselves. Still, I got around to fixing most of them, although there's still more fixes and changes to come![/p][h2]Gameplay:[/h2][p]-Dropping an item now takes a turn(sort of a bug/oversight fix more than anything, but relevant here)[/p][p]-Weapon buff talismans can now no longer be prepared (they just buffed weapons in your current slot, so it didn't work when prepared, no perfect solution for how it would choose which other slot to buff if you had multiple weapons). To compensate, they no longer take an extra turn to use when used from your inventory.[/p][p]-Ghosts and undead are now immune to instant death (such as from garrote, etc).[/p][h2]QOL:[/h2][p]-Added an FAQ entry about monsters tagging along.[/p][p]-Added a .pdf manual, located alongside the .exe. Thanks again to Dean Earwicker and Zakalwe![/p][p]-Added a "Main Menu" button to the start menu in-game.[/p][p]-Monsters stat info now displays modified values (affected by buffs/debuffs) instead of base values, with colors to indicate whether its above or below the base value.[/p][p]-Added duration info to items that have a buff duration.[/p][h2]Bugfixes:[/h2][p]-Fixed a bug where Deceive was broken.[/p][p]-Fixed(?) the issue of the exp display sometimes being wrong about whether or not you would level up.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where using + to select things on the item window caused errors with kamikui.[/p][p]-Changed a few mentions of "gold" to "silver".[/p][p]-Fixed some bugs where failing to use a calligraphy set would softlock.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where the game would say that you had unlearned scrolls when you did not.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where reading a scroll that you had learned would take a turn.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where it would say that an enemy heard you when it was just a neutral enemy.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where the "attack" command for allies was crashing.[/p][p]-Fixed some issues related to movement abilities where they would not make you face in the correct direction.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where the kamikui could prepare talismans.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.2
notes.content: [p]Another week, another patch. Nothing very glamorous in this one, I've been working on the translation pretty much full time, so a few things have fallen by the wayside. But the whole thing is going smoothly, and I've had the time to iron out a small few things here and there along the way.[/p][h2]Gameplay:[/h2][p]-No changes this patch, but will probably do more tests and adjustments soon.[/p][h2]QOL:[/h2][p]-Added back buttons to the character generation screens, and let you go back with ESC. (You could always do this by pressing backspace, but I forgot to improve it before release.)[/p][p]-Did a large internal overhaul on the mouse system. It should behave properly in all situations now![/p][h2]Bugfixes:[/h2][p]-Fixed a bug where the Bloody Tears perk was causing issues with eye abilities.[/p][p]-Fixed an issue where some of the game was partially translated when playing in Japan (this wasn't intentional, the Japanese locale is still in development and may cause errors if left on, however the game was automatically detecting the players locale and setting it)[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where using armor would take turns even when it can't be used.[/p][p]-Made it clearer that Soul Gathering is for melee sneak attacks only.[/p]

notes.title: 1.0.1 Hotfix
notes.content: [p]Just a small fix.[/p][p]-Fixed an issue where the character creation would crash when mousing over the blade flurry scroll.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 1.0.1 - Fixes and Tweaks
notes.content: [p]Shadowed's first post-release patch is not terribly exciting, just mostly fixes and tweaks. There's more to come, though! However much of my time has been spent laying the groundwork for the JP translation.[/p][h2]Gameplay:[/h2][p]-Made weasels slightly less charming.[/p][p]-Made Onigiri slightly less heavy[/p][p]-Made event rooms in forests notably rarer. [/p][h2]QOL:[/h2][p]-There is now an option to disable the mouse.[/p][p]-You can now use items in your inventory by clicking on them without having to use the "use item" command.[/p][p]-Made the mouse behave a little better in general.[/p][p]-Added a new feature where a help popup will appear to tell you about your current negative status effects and what they do. It can be dismissed, or set to not show up in game options.[/p][h2]Bugfixes:[/h2][p]-Fixed a bug that was causing a few perks not to show up in-game, most notably the Ronin's Iajutsu line.[/p][p]-Fixed the temple loot option saying it gives -20 purity when it gives -30[/p][p]-Added extra failsafes to prevent stairs from being unreachable in level generation[/p][p]-Fixed some more potential problems with the new monster warning system[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where charming monsters would not count as defeating them in a locked arena room.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where the 26 martyrs fight would end prematurely.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where unlocked doors(via bosses etc) would not let you mouse over them to open.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where becoming confused, charmed, or berserk could disable mouse movement[/p]

notes.title: Patch 0.9.95: Final overhaul, release very soon!
notes.content: [p]Shadowed is a game that has been in development for quite a while now. A lot of things have been added that weren't part of the original plan, some parts of the original plan didn't turn out so well, and many different changes have been made thanks to feedback. With all this being said, the release is *very* close, just a few days away in fact, and when I went over my core design goals, and I realized that Shadowed had strayed away from a few of them. This next patch is quite an upheaval as far as these things go, but to sum it up in a few words, most things in the game have gotten easier, although actually defeating Shuten-douji has gotten much harder. As always, the ascension modes are there for people seeking a greater challenge.[/p][p]Note: Some changes in this update may not carry over to saved games/builds. Apologies for any inconvenience.[/p][p]This post might get quite long, but I want to explain my design goals, and how they went. Starting with the good:[/p][h3]Class fantasy[/h3][p]My biggest goal with shadowed was to make a roguelike that really did things like ninja/samurai/onmyoji justice. This one, I think has gone very well.[/p][h3]Stealth matters, but combat is inevitable[/h3][p]It's been a long and hard road, but with the recent updates, I'm very happy with where stealth is in Shadowed. There are good rewards for partaking in it, and it feels good to do, but combat is still a major core focus of the game.[/p][h3]Tactical combat[/h3][p]With Shadowed, I wanted to make a roguelike where repeatedly bumping an enemy to death was rarely the optimal solution. I don't know if I would say I did a perfect job at this, but I think I did quite well, and have no regrets with how it turned out.[/p][h3]Varied enemies[/h3][p]Shadowed ended up having a lot more enemies than were originally planned. And while some of them are basic, I'm happy with this too.[/p][h3]Cool and useful status effects[/h3][p]This is one that I may have gone a little too far with, if anything. Still, there's nothing that I dislike enough to warrant changes.[/p][h3]Fun-to-explore levels[/h3][p]Here's where we get to the first one that I have some issue with. Mostly, the castle levels were still a bit dry. But beyond that, I think it's all good.[/p][h3]Every stat is good for every class[/h3][p]This was something of a failure. The stat growth system is something that I was quite attached to, but it just makes it so that you get more value for levelling some stats than others, and ironically, the fact that every stat has value meant that it was just better to level whatever got you the most stats in the end.[/p][h3]Preparation and long-term planning[/h3][p]This one is a mixed bag. I'm happy with fatigue, but preparation has been a bit of a fail. If you round a corner and run into a fire monster about to roast you, you're not going to have your fire resistance items prepared, for several reasons: Limited slots, and few ways to see enemies coming. Unfortunately, some of the issues here run quite deep, but there are at least a few steps that can be taken to make this aspect a little better.[/p][h3]Getting to Shuten is the easy part[/h3][p]This is one that most people may not even really know, but yes, my core vision was always to be having reaching Shuten be challenging, but beating him to be extremely difficult. I wanted the game to be a balancing act of trying to survive, while also trying to assemble the items/skills necessary to win. It's hard to say how well this went, but I certainly think things could be better, and I need to balance out all the buffs that the player is receiving somehow anyway.[/p][p][b]With all these in mind, you should understand the changes being made now:[/b][/p][p]-Shuten has been buffed, a lot. If you don't have countermeasures, he will obliterate you.[/p][p]-Added the "talisman of ritual binding" item. These are talismans that will weaken Shuten, and they are scattered randomly throughout the game, with a few fixed spawns. If you don't have around 10 or so of these by the end, you're gonna be in for a rough time.[/p][p]-Shuten will now patiently wait for you if you have divine sake (so he doesn't oneshot you before you can offer it to him)[/p][p]-For the Kamikui, his resistance mutations have been buffed. This should hopefully be enough to give him a fighting chance.[/p][p]-All stats now cost 3 points to level. This has been quite a painful decision, but in the end, as much as I liked the idea of the class scaling system, it just didn't really lend itself well to the "all stats for every class" thing.[/p][p]-Each class now has a "preferred stat". They get 1 of this stat every second level up. This actually maths out to being worse than A scaling for the purposes of maxing a stat, but overall, just about every character can have more stats overall now thanks to the changes.[/p][p]-Many, many, many perks and abilities have had their requirements/scaling tweaked to reflect these changes.[/p][p]-"Squishy" classes such as the Kunoichi and Onmyoji only get 2 HP per HP increase instead of the normal 3, to help maintain their identity.[/p][p]-The stats window on character generation still keeps the A-D ranking system, but it's mostly a starting stats/cosmetic thing moreso than anything else.[/p][p]-Even though the whole "six points per level and 3 to level a stat" thing could be divided down to 2 and 1 respectively, the 6 per level figure is being maintained in order to preserved the balance of stat point boosts from items/events/perks etc. It's a little inelegant, but changing it would honestly double the amount of work that this stat overhaul has taken so far.[/p][p]-Characters now have +1 prepare slots, and the second prepare slot perk no longer exists. The Kamikui is unaffected. Taking one perk for an extra slot may be an interesting decision, but I don't think it feels very good to do twice.[/p][p]-Pills now have a base use time of 0, meaning that they take 1 turn when used from inventory, and 0 turns when prepared. This *sort of* makes them better than talismans, although the same bonus could not be given to talismans without making the onmyoji absurdly powerful, so it just is what it is. Pills do still have the disadvantage of having weight and needing identification though.[/p][p]-There are now warning messages that play when dangerous monsters are near, but not in sight. The messages are quite vague, and may not help you if you don't have the right countermeasures, but it's something.[/p][p]-Castle levels have received another change. There is a new system where statues will randomly spawn in rooms and hallways, causing buffs/debuffs to enemies or allies within. Most of these start out harmful to the player (or beneficial to monsters), but may be converted to the players side with a little luck and high purity. Statues that spawn in hallways need a sacrifice, however, just to make things interesting. This was probably the biggest overhaul code-wise, so any testing and feedback is appreciated.[/p][p]Misc changes:[/p][p]-Immoral choices in events now corrupt you more.[/p][p]-Overexertion now gives you a little more fatigue to work with.[/p][p]QOL:[/p][p]-Readjusted the colors in the help docs.[/p][p]Bugfixes:[/p][p]-fixed a bug where enemy spells were not affected by damage debuffs.[/p][p]-fixed a bug related to the game not knowing if you were inside a room/hallway or not(may have been responsible for arena rooms bugging out)[/p][p]-fixed a bug where taking and deselecting items on character generation stopped working sometimes.[/p][p]-fixed a bug where you would get a "you cant use that" message after successfully using poison.[/p][p]-cleaned up some edge cases where passages in castle levels could spawn in inappropriate places[/p][p][/p][h3]Thank you for supporting Shadowed! The final release will be next weekend, but don't worry, there will be post-launch support. The Japanese translation is also on the way![/h3]

notes.title: Patch 0.9.92
notes.content: [p]Shadowed's next patch comes with bugfixes, QoL, and some minor balance changes. The game is in its home stretch, and there will be some pretty big balance changes to come, but this patch is more focused on polishing things up a bit. [/p][h2]Gameplay:[/h2][p]-Re-nerfed the bow a little after some more testing. Also nerfed the Iga's conservation perk a bit, and buffed the Volley perk.[/p][p]-Forest levels now have measures in place to prevent too few and too many monsters from spawning.[/p][p]-Relaxed the purity requirement for the god statue event.[/p][p]-Adjusted Tesso, Iron Rat slightly.[/p][p]-Talismans can now be used as long as they are identified. The same auto-ID system based on spirit is now in place, but it only affects the auto ID now. This is mostly to cut down on confusion, but also make high-level talismans potentially useful and make ID'ing things more desirable.[/p][p]-Reduced the fatigue costs of combat a little. The fatigue cost of moving is now a flat value instead of scaling with your carry weight.[/p][h2]QOL:[/h2][p]-Changed the sizes of some elements on the character screen[/p][p]-Added a "large resolution mode" in the graphics options, which should help with larger screen sizes.[/p][p]-Added a graphics option for contrast as well.[/p][p]-Items in starting item selector are now sorted according to point cost.[/p][h2]Bugfixes:[/h2][p]-Fixed a bug where vision cones would remain on non-combat levels[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where the bow would display a small AOE with arrows[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where items would become white when selected then deselected in character generation[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where the bonus HP from ascension caused monster health bars to not work properly[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where artifacts were actually spawning MORE commonly rather than less.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where Breath failing due to status effects would consume your ki anyway.[/p][p]-Fixed several bugs where enemies would shoot you through walls.[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where certain kamikui perks would stay ranked up after death.[/p][p]-Fixed the bug where certain things wouldn't trigger properly when hasted(such as self explosions from wounds).[/p][p]-Fixed a bug where monsters would smell you while asleep.[/p][p]-Fixed some issues where monsters could see you at odd times/places.[/p][p]-Fixed(?) an issue where saves may not have been deleting on death.[/p]

notes.title: Patch 0.9.91
notes.content:
Shadowed's new patch comes with a bevvy of minor changes.

About the recent saving/loading issues: Fixing these is my top priority. This patch *should* fix it. These issues were quite bizarre because everything worked on the test build, the desktop build, the steam client version(on my work computer), the desktop of my other computer, but *not* the steam client version of my other computer. The solution unfortunately means that any builds/saves you have will be deleted, but you may recover your builds if you dig them out of your [game]/saves/data folder and transplant them to users/user/appdata/roaming/godot/Shadowed/builds/. Apologies for any inconvenience.

[h2]Gameplay:[/h2]
-Retooled item spawning. Artifacts and strong weapons are rarer, and when artifacts do spawn, they try to respect the current floor more often.
-Changed the Ox's Vitality perk, it now simply gives HP-8 bonus HP upon taking it.
-Arrow break chance is now 25%, down from 50%.
-Added two new monsters, the Bandit Archer, and Abandoned Quiver. These enemies will drop a small amount of arrows on death.
-Added a new technique, Surge. Most of the classes who don't normally use Ki have it. It uses 1 ki to grant some minor benefits to spellcasting.
-Added a few new mutations.
-Adjusted a few things with Kamikui. Centipedes now costs fatigue. The HP cost of Power Through Pain is now 1.
-Looting shrines now creates noise (in addition to the aggro it could normally cause).
-Relaxed and improved the rules for Innocent Monster.

[h2]QOL:[/h2]
-Changed the text in the help docs to be less eye-straining. The help docs will also automatically disable the CRT screen effect when you are in them in order to reduce blur.
-Added a bar that can be used to resize the size of the help doc window.
-Added an option for brightness.

[h2]Bugfixes:[/h2]
-Hopefully fixed the issues related to saving and loading and builds crashing. 
-Fixed a bug where attacking any monster ever would trigger redemption loss. (Honestly no idea how that one slipped by.)
-Fixed some typos.
-Fixed some miscellaneous things being wrong in character generation.
-Fixed a bug where Shifting Soul could give useless "Blood" essence(this was cut, or rather was supposed to be)
-Fixed a bug where sleeping monsters would never wake up due to noise
-Fixed holy monsters sometimes not counting as enemies to the kamikui for targeting purposes
-Holy ground in shrines now works in the forest(it was always supposed to, just bugged)
-Fixed the moon event art not showing up.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.6 - Level 12 perks and various fixes
notes.content:
Shadowed's latest update comes with level 12 perks - You can only pick one, but they are very, very powerful, and should help make Shuten a lot more manageable. There have also been a few more features and fixes. We're getting close to release now!

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added level 12 perks! A lot of these are game-changers!
-Added a few more miscellaneous fun perks that I forgot to add before.
-Added an achievement
-Shadowblood ninpo no longer stacks.
-Slightly buffed Purifying Salt's damage.
-Charmed monsters no longer hit you with their AOE abilities.


[b]QOL:[/b]
-Fixed some typos
-The Look command now automatically goes to the nearest monster.
-Finally added a radius indicator for target abilities with a radius.
-Added better messages for when an ally dies.
-Improved enemy AI, in regards to how your allies behave and how enemies react to them

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug with the Ghost of Ooe achievement
-Fixed a bug where the crafting table could drop stacksize -1 items that could be sold infinitely
-Fixed spirit poison still being called spoison in message window
-Fixed the Heretic perk still having its old drawback
-Fixed a bug where enemies would display abilities with a negative cooldown
-Fixed a bug where the game would crash upon trying to leave spawn with a build.
-Fixed a bug where selecting a Kunoichi build would crash
-Fixed a bug where selecting a build would make all items have a negative stacksize
-Fixed the issue where adjacent monsters would sometimes be hidden then they weren't supposed to be

notes.title: Patch 0.9.5: Achievements and extra
notes.content:
Achievements are here! There's not much to say about them, some of them may be pretty tough for a completionist, but hopefully nothing too brutal. They should also help serve as a way to keep track of how far the average player makes it into Shadowed, as well.
Additionally, I got around to fixing a few more minor issues. Level 12 perks are finally up next!

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added achievements.
-Changed Shuten slightly, his powered-up form now corrupts on attack.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Changed the blend mode of the character's sprite, it should now show up better when wounded on the hell levels. This may cause it to have odd colors in rare situations though.
-Added a note in the tutorial about being able to resize the UI.
-Overhauled some internal things, which should now prevent your settings from being reset every time I mess with settings in a patch. If there is another reset, it should be the final one.
-"spoison" now displays as "S.Poison".
-Added a stats window into the main menu where you can check your ascension progress and a few other things.
-Fixed some more typos.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where pills were not having the correct sprite.
-Fixed(?) an issue where Path of War may not have been giving perk points.
-Fixed(?) an issue where the left side menu would randomly shrink.
-Fixed an exploit where you could order an ally to attack a kiting monster and the kiting monster would not retaliate.
-Monsters that spawn from the eggs event will now become hostile to everything if they were non-aggressive.
-Allied monsters will now turn when struck, instead of getting back/side attacked repeatedly for no reason.
-Fixed an issue where ascension 7 Iga was permanently yellow due to HP values.
-Fixed a bug that may have been causing higher/lower scores than expected.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.4 - Ascension, difficulty and easy modes!
notes.content:
Patch 0.9.4 comes with Shadowed's brand new Ascension system! Not only will you be able to ramp up the difficulty on repeat playthroughs, but "cheat" easymode options have been added as well, many of which can help new players learn the ropes. Of course, you're not eligible for any unlocks while using the easy options, but you can't have everything. Easy mode options include things like being able to retry from your last save, seeing enemy vision cones, doubled inventory space and less weight, learning all techniques and spells, ignoring perk requirements, and more, so there's plenty to play around with! A few more miscellaneous improvements have been made as well. 

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added the Ascension system!
-Prettied up the title menus a bit. More improvements to come!
-Shuten-douji has been nerfed somewhat, but these nerfs are undone in one of the new ascension modes.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Build picker in character gen has now had its readability improved drastically.
-Fixed some more typos.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where when eating meat, 2 would be eaten at once.
-Fixed an issue where taking the Herbalist perk would not identify pills that were already in your inventory.
-Fixed a bug where messages for exploding monsters were incorrect.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.3 - New wound system, new perks, big rebalance
notes.content:
A huge patch coming in, Shadowed's combat and builds have evolved! Shadowed now has a wound system, the goals of which are as follows:
-Make combat more difficult/costly for frail classes, while making classes like the Ronin feel more suited towards direct fights.
-Add more long-term thinking and strategizing. Getting heavily wounded before a boss fight can cost you a run!
-Make certain items more useful.
-Be relatively simple to understand. All the wound system does is lower your max regen total, there's not much more to it than that.

In addition, Shadowed has received a large perk rebalance and additions, with the main core goal of helping out the ninja classes, and making it so there are no bad perks. Many of the "core" omniclass perks have been buffed or reworked entirely, ninjas in general have a few new things, and the Shinobi, Iga, and Kunoichi all now have a suite of new perks to make them feel more distinct and bring them more in line with the other three classes. It's too much to get into here, so you'll have to play around with them yourself!
Finally, a few bugfixes and QOL changes have been made as well.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added the wound system. This system makes combat deadlier for many low-health classes, as well as increasing the threat of certain enemies and making bosses potentially more difficult. Wounds can be cured with the poultice item, baths, and the vitality pill.
-Exhaustion no longer affects your max heal regen total.
-Rebalanced many bad perks across the board, with a focus on omni-class perks and ninja perks in particular. Many, many buffs and reworks abound, but a few small nerfs here and there also.
-Monk now gets the perk that prevents ki from decaying fast when out of combat for free, in order to help him use stances more often.
-Player now takes 2x damage from holy instead of 3x.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-You can no longer rest or perform certain repeated actions when statused (to prevent the game locking you and repeating the action until death when poisoned/etc)
-Stairs and events that you haven't completed now glow while on the minimap.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where dying due to corruption in an event would freeze.
-Fixed the "repeat last" action (n key) not being in the rebind menu.
-Fixed a bug where some accuracy and dodge buffs weren't actually doing anything.
-Fixed an issue where the N key could not be rebound.
-Fixed a bug where the turn counter didn't save.
-Fixed(?) some issues relating to resting.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.25: Crafting finishing touches, new additions, much balancing
notes.content:
As a continuation of last patch, more general balance and item changes abound. As it turned out, the crafting table was also somehow even buggier than I thought, but should *hopefully* be all good now, and much more has been done to improve the experience and let you use crafting to minimize wasted inventory space. In addition, a slew of minor balance changes and game additions have been made.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-A-rank stat scaling now costs 2.5 stat points instead of 2, and D-rank scaling is now 4.5 instead of 5. A-rank scaling previously seemed to make leveling the stat a no-brainer, even if you're building for something else, and D-rank scaling was very punishing. Having to bringing decimals into the system is unfortunate, but it was either that or I would have to increase all stat point gains across the board and work something else out, which would have been a lot more finicky to implement, and basically the same in practice.
-Readjusted the classes' stat growths and starting slots.
-Added special one-way passage tiles into the castle to spice up exploration a bit! Also added some more hiding floors.
-Undid the movement change to the Akaname(it was trivially easy to fight)
-Laid some groundwork for an upcoming wound system.
--Added two items, the Medicinal herbs and the Poultice. Herbs are relatively common and can cure some useful ailments, poultices are rare and are used for out-of-combat healing. Poultices can be crafted into to curing pills if you don't want them.
-Rebalanced many event rewards with more feedback, testing, and new items in mind. Some "bad" options have been buffed, and many "no brainer" options have been nerfed. Options which require specific classes/perks/items are still generally the best.
-Seduction now no longer triggers exertion.
-Added art for the crafting tables.
-Made shop events rarer.
-Added a new forest event, the Kodama Village. It's quite rare, but gives good rewards. This will probably be the last new event.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Reworked the crafting table somewhat, to help it align more with the core goal of reducing clutter. You can now craft many foods into onigiri, berries into pickles, and also exchange resistance pills for talismans and vice versa, albeit with a failure chance.
-Shops now always stock rice, to aid in food crafting.
-Fixed a bunch of scroll-related errors where going upwards from the top would select the bottom option but not correctly scroll the container
-Added a toggle to craft menu that filters out uncraftable recipes
-Added a top "leave" option to the craft table, so that you don't accidentally craft the top option when mashing the craft button too much

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed an exploit where you could craft large amounts of small bombs.
-Fixed an issue with descriptions in crafting menu.
-Fixed an issue with multiples of the same scroll showing up in the shops.
-Fixed a bug where crafting a stimulant/other unknown pill would not identify it
-Fixed a bug where crafting items with a full inventory would not drop the item.
-Fixed a bug where monsters could walk through sealed doors sometimes.
-Fixed a bug relating to crafting items by pressing keys.
-Fixed a bug where bear traps and caltrops couldn't be used without the mechanics perk.
-Fixed a bug where failing to use a trap would break the UI.
-Fixed a bug where the Ronin's stealth would be wrong if he made a premade build with the stealthy perk.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.20: Banks, Inventory management, and balancing
notes.content:
This next patch mostly comes with balancing and housekeeping. Measures have been taken to reduce inventory clutter, make the decision of what to take and not take with you more tactical and less repetitive, and overall make Shadowed's later levels feel more about quality and less about quantity. Some QoL changes and bugfixes have been made as well.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added the bank. These can be found in baths, next to shops. They will let you deposit and withdraw items later, but charge a small fee to deposit.
-Inventory size is now 26.
-Paralyze can no longer immobilize you for multiple turns in a row(this was meant to be changed when stun was changed this way, but it slipped my mind).
-Substantially reduced the spawn rate of many rooms in the Castles that gave a lot of loot
-Heavily retooled the spawn rates and levels of monsters in the Castles, evening things out and making higher-level enemies more likely to appear (instead of mobs of low levels)
-Readjusted critical rates and damage for very light weapons.
-Adjusted the level curve to make it harder to go up levels around the midgame.
-Added art for the water dragon's shrine event.
-Nerfed a few poisonous monsters by making their movements erratic.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Made it clearer in the help files that the monk can use ritual to get into stances quickly.
-Updated the UI to better reflect how and what Exhaustion is doing.
-Changed some colors so that your fatigue number is more readable at high fatigue(I.E much less dark).
-Substantially improved performance for allied monsters, as well as monsters in general.
-Added an auto white/blacklist feature for autopickup: Dropping an item will blacklist it from autopickup, and manually picking one up will whitelist it. Heavy items like swords are not whitelisted.


[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a rare issue that may have been causing crashes in the forest levelgen.
-Fixed some other issues that may have been causing crashes.
-Fixed an issue where neutral monsters that were attacked by other enemies would become untargetable by enemies and go on rampages unchecked
-Fixed an issue that cause you to not be able to use items from the bag while slightly blind(was changed a while ago, but I missed a spot)
-Fixed an issue where Ki would diminish when performing 0-turn actions.
-Fixed(?) an extremely rare bug where items would spawn in walls in the forest
-Fixed a bug where force resting exertion didn't deduct fatigue

notes.title: Patch 0.9.12: Miscellaneous balance, QoL, and fixes
notes.content:
A big bugfix and QoL patch, with some balancing too. As it turns out, the last patch may have been a tad rushed, but aside from fixing that, there are a fair few more changes as well. Some more clutter/inventory changes will be coming in the next patch.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Reworked stealth yet again. Since enemy vision was fixed last patch, it became a bit too easy again.
---Making noise(such as by fighting) near enemies who are searching will alert them.
---Fighting temporarily reduces your VISSTEALTH to 0.
---Searching(yellow) enemies will be more sensitive to sound in general.
---Adjusted the chance for monsters to see you.
---Monsters now check their vision at the end of their turn rather than the start (makes certain things a bit clearer).
-Smoke bomb radius reduced from 3 to 2. Damage from damaging bombs has been reduced across the board.
-Reduced the size of the castle levels. This may make them a bit easier, but also cut down on clutter, tedium, and increase performance.
-Inventory is now limited to 30 items. This is a bandaid fix for inventory clutter for now, but more will be done about this soon.
-Made certain monsters (mostly uniques) a bit rarer.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-The crafting recipe list now refreshes properly when crafting something that can craft into something else.
-Pressing escape in an event that has a "leave" option will auto-select that option.
-Clicking on the main character will now attempt to get items on the floor.
-Clicking on a slot should swap to that slot

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Improved general game performance (most notably in castle)
-Fixed artifact item sprites being wrong or missing
-Fixed an issue where the bottom buttons of events wouldn't click with the mouse
-Fixed a bug where you could craft infinite shurikens
-Fixed a bug where recipes wouldn't give the right amount of output
-Fixed(?) some issues related to enemy effects doing damage at the wrong time and/or crashing upon death
-Adjusted the size of the shop sidebar to avoid clipping
-Fixed a few random crashes
-Fixed(?) an issue where purple light would show up upon death in some cases.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.10: Crafting table, QOL, and bugfixes
notes.content:
Introducing the crafting campfire! While it may seem like a strange idea, there's a lot of neat things to do with it, most notably letting ninja turn negative pills into poisons, making rice and other foods more useful, converting between mines and bombs, and potentially giving a few other useful options as well. I also have some more uses planned for a potential future update, but with that being said, I'm not planning on taking crafting much further or trying to turn it into anything more than a minor feature, as the goal of adding it was to make junk more useful, not add even more junk in! So you don't have to worry, I have no plans to turn the game into a survival craft.
Some much-needed QOL and bugfixes are here as well.
EDIT: Had to make a small hotfix to 0.9.11, accidentally forgot to enable the crafting tables!

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added crafting camps, these are found in the same rooms as baths.
-Added numerous new poisons. Ninja may now craft these out of negative pills.
-Poisons now weigh a bit less.
-Bombs now require throwing proficiency in order to be used properly. The still have a 1/3 chance to work without it, but may otherwise either be lost or get thrown without detonating.
-Added art for the Forge, God statue, Kappa

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Reworked weapon swapping AP costs somewhat, and added a display on your slots that shows how much AP a swap will take. The "rework" is more of an internal code thing than a game mechanics thing, there were actually many strange behaviors that the old swapping system had that are now fixed or otherwise easier to understand.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where food-eating monsters could swallow your sake jugs whole.
-Fixed some issues related to weapon swapping.
-Potentially fixed a bug where the mouse would stay on screen instead of fading and potentially cause jumping around when using the arrow keys
-Fixed some issues with stealth(again) where enemies had eyes in the back of their head.

notes.title: Patch 0.9.0 : The Onmyoji's Debut
notes.content:
Rather suddenly, the Onmyoji is here! I originally intended to lay a little basic groundwork from him in this patch, but in the end, I got a little bit carried away and ended up taking the time to just put him in the game for real. It probably was a little bit poorly timed, but at least now, I will be able to make future balance changes with every class in mind, and if you play him a bit, you'll probably understand why I couldn't leave him alone once I started. After this however, I will be returning to more frequent patches with QOL and other mechanics updates, and I apologize for the slowness of the recent patches.

As for the Onmyoji himself, he's a blast! Fans of Vancian magic will enjoy him a lot, as will people who just like Onmyojis, and if you're like me and like both, he just might end up being your favorite. Balance-wise, he's a class of great strengths and great weaknesses, which I think makes for a fun dynamic overall, and he inherently has a variety of playstyles available. Bamboozle your way through levels with memory erasure and invisibility, nuke down enemies with elemental magic, summon familiars, or buff yourself and fight directly! Even without getting into his perks, he's a lot of fun, although quite a glass cannon.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added the Onmyoji!
-Added spirit requirements for talismans back into the game, and rebalanced them.
-Calligraphy is finally in the game. The Onmyoji starts with it, but other classes will need a perk + the calligraphy set, as it is quite powerful.
-Added the Obliviation talisman, which can cause a monster to forget you, as well as many other Onmyoji-only talismans and shikigami.
-Made the Okuri-inu a bit rarer.
-Added the [QUICK] keyword to the warfan.
-Made talismans slightly more common drops in general.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Fixed a few typos.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where the [MYSTIC] weapon tag did nothing.
-Improved the "stay at a distance" AI so it doesn't just sit there if the player can safely kill them with ranged attacks.
-Fixed a bug where being hasted would act as though you skipped turns in some strange ways

notes.title: Patch 0.8.2 - Enemy overhaul, 30+ new monsters, and more!
notes.content:
It's been a while! This new patch is pretty huge, as it has a few things that were meant to be in the last patch(before it was cut short by a hotfix), as well as huge, final batch of new enemies! This has been a long time coming, and not having the enemy roster finished has made it pretty tough for me to make balance decisions, and the later levels in the game in particular were in a pretty bad way enemy-wise. It took longer than anticipated to add everything, but now I feel that it's in a very good spot.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added in 6 new bosses, 3 for each boss floor. These have some very unique fights, such as one who can clone himself, a horde boss, a long-ranged tentacle octopus who can toss you away from him, and more!
-Added in over 30 new enemies in general, many of which are lategame enemies. The forest levels should be largely the same, although they got a bunch of new enemies a while ago.
-Added many new uniques, some in particular having some very unique behavior.
-Rebalanced some enemies. Notably, some enemies can now inflict corruption while attacking. Accuracy values have also been lowered a little across the board, dodge feels a bit too weak for many of the classes. EXP values have also been adjusted.
-Some enemies can now "kite" the player by keeping distance from them. Some enemies can also now melee attack 2-3 range. Many new abilities have also been added. Some old enemies have been retrofitted with these.

---[b]Other gameplay changes[/b]:
-Changed how caltrops work. They are now a stackable item with a chance to break instead of a uses-based item.
-The chilled status effects now prevents enemies from exploding upon death.
-Monsters now make noise upon moving, even on non-noisy tiles, which the player can potentially hear. The chance depends on the monster's weight.
-Added a perk that can boost the player's hearing substantially.
-Slightly nerfed Shinobi Armor. It now reduces dodge by 10%. (Enemy accuracy has been lowered a bit, and the shinobi already had enough defensive ability as it was) 
-Added a few new artifacts, which are dropped by specific uniques.
-Made some very minor adjustments to the costs of starting items.
-Added artwork for the shops(very cute!).

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Did another (hopefully final) adjustment to improve visibility for items/enemies, especially in places like the castle. It was tough to come up with a blanket solution to make enemies more visible, and if people don't like the current implementation, tell me and I'll put in an option to turn it off.
-Added sounds for when ranged attacks hit.
-The inventory panel can now be dragged to expand or shrink it.
-Improved enemy descriptions. They now state if a monster has on-death effects like explosions or not.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where enemies would become stuck when there was a 1-tile object in between the player and the monster
-Fixed a bug where Tamamo wouldn't drop her unique robe

notes.title: Patch 0.8.1 - QOL, minor changes, hotfix
notes.content:
With the monk finally released, I've had a lot of housekeeping to do. This patch has a lot of bugfixes, QOL adjustments, and small gameplay changes, in order to help sort things out for larger changes to come. I wanted to do a little more before patching, but due to a rather serious crash, I had to push this one out a bit early. So next patch will have a few more things like this as well.

Note- This patch introduces some new game options, so your current options may be reset. Apologies for any inconvenience.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added the Rice food item. This will replace a lot of food drops, in order to balance out the food economy somewhat. More things are planned for it down the line.
-Reworked exertion a little bit. Exertion is now multiplied for each turn in a row that you used an exerting ability. The point of exertion was to punish spamming spells repeatedly, and it wasn't doing a great job of that, hence the changes. I may have to take another look at fatigue costs later however, the new system may be too punishing. 
-Overhauled the final bath event. Bathing costs less corruption, options will be disabled if the corruption would kill you, purifying grants EXP, and there is now a "drink" option that gets you to level 12 but corrupts you by 15 for each level.
-Traps now cannot be set unless you have the "mechanics" perk, which currently only ninja have access to (and start with). Caltrops and bear traps may still be used without this perk.
-Fixed/implemented bear traps. They will now spawn more frequently, which should hopefully reduce the amount of smoke mines also.

-Added unique art for the large fountain event.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Added ghost arrows that indicate which way enemies are about to turn. Very nice for stealth!
-Using ranged attacks now displays (ranged) on the UI to make the accuracy/damage/crit values clearer.
-Added colors to status effect strings in the status window.
-The info window at the bottom of the screen is now fully draggable and resizable. This may cause some issues if you resize the screen resolution, but there's now an option to reset it.
-Added a message that makes it more obvious that monks start with +1 perk point.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where taking a Mastery scroll at game start would result in crashes.
-Fixed a bug where looking at something would need multiple tries to update the window.
-Attempted to fix the bug where killing enemies with explosions could cause bombs they dropped on death to explode.
-Fixed a bug where the player would not automatically face toward confused/omnihostile enemies.
-Fixed the issue where monsters would look strange and not be able to be examined on the first turn they spawned in.
-Attempted to fix an issue where certain rooms in the castle could be blocked off in rare circumstances

notes.title: Patch 0.8.00: The Monk Arrives!
notes.content:
It's been a while, but it's here! After a lot of work, the Monk is finally released! With his special Stance mechanic, his stances all have entrance, exit, and passive effects, which allow him to do a great many things when combined or by themselves. He is also adept at using prayer beads, purifying salt, and to a lesser extent, sake.
Numerous smaller gameplay tweaks have been made as well.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-The monk is finally here! He has a unique stance mechanic, and quite a few quirks, such as starting with 2 perk points and having buffed prayer beads. There's a lot of stance combinations and synergies to try out, and he can be built in many different ways.

Other:
-You cannot be stunned for two turns in a row. The stun value will persist, however, so you can still get stunned again if the stun value is large, and you will still be vulnerable even if you can act.
-Changed how spirit poison works for enemies. It now gives them a 40+spoison*3% chance to fail any non-cure ability.
-Enemies inflicted with berserk now cannot deal any damage type except poison and physical while attacking.
-Curing blind now updates your vision radius properly that turn.
-Adjusted the formula for block while unarmed.
-Increased the fatigue costs of ninpo somewhat.
-Added a new weapon, Jumonji spear. This polearm can only be properly wielded by a monk.
-Adjusted how much sake you get from refilling a jug at a barrel event.

-Added art for the demon bell and barrel events.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Updated the help docs.


[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed an issue with the Ronin's Spirit Cohesion potentially not working.
-Fixed a bug where charm stopped you from casting any spell.
-Fixed a bug where purifying salt did much more damage than intended.

notes.title: Patch 0.7.06 - Full mouse support
notes.content:
This is a fairly small patch, but one that finally adds mouse-based movement! Beyond that, the reason it's so small is because I've mostly been focusing on adding the Monk, who is coming along nicely. Still, any feedback realated to the new mouse system is appreciated.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Laid a lot of groundwork for the monk.
-You can now use items while partially blind(but not fully blind).

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Added full mouse support for movement. You will still need the keyboard to summon menus and the like, but outside of this, everything in the game can be done with the mouse now.
-The spot trap message now logs what kind of trap it is.


[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Updated the tutorials and fixed a potential crash within them.
-Fixed a bug where spells/attacks could be targeted through interactibles, resulting in strange behaviors.

notes.title: Patch 0.7.05 - Item rework, artifacts, huge QoL, and more!
notes.content:
The item rework is finally here! There are now many changes that should hopefully make inventory management much less painful. Not only that, but artifacts have finally been added to the game as well, and there are a few tweaks to the castle levels too.
Additionally, I ended up going on a QoL rampage this patch. I'm very excited about some of the changes there, and the game is now more playable than ever. I feel like it's in a very good state for me to put some time aside and start focusing on the next class, the Monk.
Note: This update introduces new game options, and thus will reset your options. Apologies for any inconvenience.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Castle tweaks:
--Made rooms smaller on average.
--Added in the arena room. This will block your path until you deal with a miniboss.
--Added in the vault. These are packed with monsters, but have some very nice rewards...

-Items:
--Completely overhauled the system for forcing good spawns. Monsters/rooms/events that are supposed to spawn good items will actually always do so now.
--Removed many redundant talismans from the game(almost all had an equivalent pill), in order to prevent inventory bloat. 
--Scrolls and talismans spawn more rarely in general.
--Artifacts have finally been implemented! Some of them have technically been in the game for a while, but there are more now, and they actually do what they say they do.
--Artifacts will also be a little bit more common now.

-Other:
--Focus now only works if there is an adjacent enemy. It also expires when combat ends.
--Broadspears now have a special keyword that lets them ignore STR requirements. The Spearwoman perk has been changed slightly.
--The Water Dragon Orb no longer works on noncombat floors(baths etc).
--The first bath is now a full bath that restores all fatigue.
--Added art for the Dojo, fountains, Blood Pool and Diviner.
--Temporarily removed Calligraphy from the game, since it doesn't do anything yet.
--The Ninja Initiate's blink now has a longer cooldown.
--Buffed Mizuto, servant of the water dragon slightly.
--The Ronin now begins with the Regenerator perk, to help his earlygame and his fatigue problems in general. To compensate for this, the perk has been toned down quite a bit(it was actually a lot more powerful than intended earlier).
--Nerfed bomb workshops slightly.

[b]QOL:[/b]
Huge changes!
-Items are now color-coded in inventory, to make things more readable.
-Autopickups now trigger after events and when monsters drop things under you.
-"Preparing an item" UI now only filters your inventory if you have more than 20 items. There are also now options to make it permanent again or never filter.
-Perks are now sorted by level and class. The perk window now has a tab system where you can scroll between groups of perks(magic-related, item-related,etc).
-Running now tries to stop before corners, interactibles, and is no longer interrupted by neutral monsters.
-Smoke mines are no longer picked up automatically.
-There is now a message when a monster comes into view. There are also options to pause when this happens, including one that only pauses when a dangerous monster is seen.
-The current force-rest system has been replaced with a traditional "choose how many turns to rest" system. The number entered also defaults to your current exertion if you have any, so it's still useful for that purpose.
-Changed the item/monster description font.
-Redid the descriptions for how monsters drop items.
-In the monster descriptions, monster cooldowns will be in red if the ability is on cooldown, and green if the monster can use it. It also displays the number.
-Fixed some more typos.


[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where traps weren't hidden properly after loading a savegame. (It didn't occur to me that it could be caused by loading, so I thought this was already fixed for a long time. Whoops!)
-Fixed a bug where crocodiles spawned by the eggs event would fall asleep.
-Fixed the doors that seal the garden middle arena during the water dragon fight having the wrong tiles.
-Fixed some issues with item/monster descriptions.
-Quality weapons/armor now sell for more silver than normal.

notes.title: Patch 0.7.04 - The new Garden
notes.content:
Happy new year! With a new year comes new levels, and Shadowed's level touchups continue. The garden is now the main focus with many improvements this patch, and the castle may be looked at a little bit next update. However, there will definitely be some much-needed changes to item spawning and QOL next patch, so look forward to it!

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-The garden rework!
--Added water channels to the garden. These can help you get around the garden quickly while alleviating some of the frustration of the maze-like construction. Watch out for aquatic creatures though!
--Channels form a square near the edges of a level. Large rooms in the center of the dungeon may also now spawn.
--Large middle rooms have 4 special variants:
--The large fountain: Make a wish, or grab some cash.
--The statue: Recieve the war god Bishamonten's blessings.
--The bell tower: Ring the bell to aggro all enemies, and recieve a reward based on the threat. Or play it safe for some items.
--The water dragon's palace: Are you brave(stupid) enough to try and take the water dragon's orb?
--The traveling onmyoji can now spawn in the garden.
--Another new event, the friendly(?) kappa, has been added to the garden rooms as well.
--The garden now has fewer, but higher-level enemies, to differentiate it from other level types.
--Added the giant frog, crocodile, and crocobear enemies
-Nerfed Purifying Salt a bit.
-Added art for apothecary, lone weapon, and egg nest events

QOL:
-Fixed some more typos.

Bugfixes:
-Fixed an issue with tile descriptions being broken in garden.
-Fixed an issue with noise being too noisy in the garden.
-Fixed several rare crashes
-Improved enemy pathfinding somewhat

notes.title: Patch 0.7.03 - Forest rework and more!
notes.content:
Shadowed's latest patch brings the forest rework! It's still a hellish place filled with beasts, but at least there's now a bit more variety!
Something else to note, there was a bug that was stopping enemies with high movespeed from actually moving and attacking on the same turn. It's also possible that it was causing other movement-related issues (such as getting stuck in places) as well. I usually wouldn't mention a bugfix here, but thanks to this being fixed, many enemies are substantially more dangerous now than they were before. I knew about this bug for a long time, but since one of the new events involves having to run away from dangerous monsters, I recently investigated it again and was able to fix it. It may be a bit of a bump in difficulty, but things were always meant to be this way. Let me know if you think that certain monsters are too unfair after this change.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Added a new food item, eggs. They are a cheap, medium-healing food.
-Revamped the forest levels. They now include clearings with a chance of events, most of which are new!
-New events include: 
--Nests where you can find eggs
--A forge where you can upgrade a weapon(!)
--The "oni party". You can get sake and EXP here, but it may not be as easy as it seems...
--The full moon (very pretty)
--The suspiciously amazing weapon that's just sitting there, just take it!
--The graveyard(also has loot, but watch out for ghosts!)
--Regular shrines can spawn here also.
-Note however, that a lot of these events are somewhat rare. But I think that this will help keep repetitions of the first few levels more interesting in the long run.
-Additionally, randomly placed loot in forests is rarer, and there are fewer monsters there overall. The chance of events should help balance these things out though, and make the forest levels a bit less brutal and more fun to explore.
-Some new enemies have been added, although they are just more low-level beasts for the forest. Again though, this should help with earlygame variety (tired of dogs and cats yet?).
-Honey is now rarer, as bears only spawn in forest clearings now. Its sell price has gone up to reflect this.
-Added graphics for the drunk oni event, scribe station event, and ninja workshop event.
-Slightly nerfed the Akaname and Centipede larva's poisons.
-Adjusted the Ronin so he starts with 3 curing pills always. Took away a dried fish to compensate.
-Stealing from the wealth shrine gives less gold and is now a bit more dangerous.

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Updated the "holding dual weapon" warning messages to "holding 2-hand weapon"
-Updated the message in the key remap window to better explain certain issues and behaviors.
-Entering a build name/character name will now automatically highlight the text for easier deletion.
-Can now exit the map screen by pressing enter.
-Changed the color of the stairs so they will stand out on the minimap more compared to other interactibles.
-Your character now turns yellow when below 70% HP.
-Fixed some more typos.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed minor issues with scrolling through start menus
-Fixed the aforementioned monster movement bug
-Fixed a bug where the thirsty oni event would say you had the war oath perk when you did not
-Fixed an issue where equipped armours would not automatically apply their effects if using a saved build(causing things like the Shinobi's visstealth to be 2)
-Fixed an issue where certain enemies spawned through events would attack themselves if confused

Stay tuned, the garden rework is on the way next!

notes.title: Patch 0.7.02
notes.content:
Happy holidays! Shadowed's latest patch has a few balance changes, rebindable keys, and many fixes!

After some more testing, the Ronin's accuracy problems were worse than anticipated. The ninja gets +20% accuracy as part of their base NINJA perk, and as it turns out, having/lacking that perk makes quite a huge difference in the early game. It doesn't really feel right that a ninja is better at melee combat than a Ronin, and as such, a few adjustments have been made there.
Food has also been slightly problematic. Players were able to get more than I thought would actually be obtainable, so things have been adjusted a little, although a rework will be coming in the future.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Nerfed the NINJA perk to only give +10% accuracy
-Nerfed a lot of early monster's DODGE by 10%, so there shouldn't be much of a difference there
-Increased the amount of ACC you get from PRE from 1 to 1.3
-The Ronin now has a new perk, Persistent Rhythm. This is available at level 1 and should help with early combat if you wish to take it, as well as having some interesting synergy.
-Gourmand has been changed. Instead of increasing fatigue restoration, it now heals HP equal to half the fatigue restoration value. Given the time cost of eating food, it's likely never worth it to eat in combat, but there are niche situations where it may still be helpful. The bonus it gives to sake is unchanged, so it may still be a good choice for the Ronin overall.
-Fatigue restoration from cooked meat and onigiri have been dropped slightly(about 2 points each).
-Added art for shrine events, cave stairs, and more

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Added rebindable keys! The problems with foreign keyboards should finally be over, or at least manageable.
-Significantly improved the help docs, specifically the block one. It has now been renamed to "derived stats" and includes a better section on block as well as dodge.
-Added in a game option to warn you/confirm before yelling
-Adjusted the camera slightly to make it more closely bound to the player when moving up or down.
-Renamed the [DUAL] keyword to [2HAND], in order to avoid confusion with the Dual weapon subtype.
-Fixed some more typos.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where the oni event would check for and drink your divine sake
-Fixed incorrect tooltips on various ki-related UI elements
-Fixed an incorrect error message when inventory was full
-Fixed ninja yells being too quiet
-Fixed an issue with the garrote technique not working
-Attempted to fix an issue with enemies that are aggro'd to join the player following the player around
-Attempted to fix an issue with enemies repeatedly bashing doors

notes.title: Patch 0.7.01 - Small changes
notes.content:
Small hotfix. Some minor gameplay changes have been made, though.

Gameplay:

notes.title: Patch 0.6.07 - Weapon technique rework!
notes.content:
Coming out with another very large patch. Some initial groundwork has been laid for the Ronin, and in doing so, the Ki system is now in the game, and will be available to all characters as part of the new weapon technique rework!
Previously, weapon techniques were being used rarely, or being spammed, with no real in-between. My vision for them was that they would compliment playstyles, but sadly it seems that they either tend to become the playstyle, or players don't bother with them at all. Letting classes have the ki system kills a lot of birds with one stone, making combat more dynamic, putting a fair limit on techniques(and thus letting them be more powerful), as well as encouraging the player to use them by having them miss out on a free resource if they don't. Some perks and support for ninja to use the system better will come eventually, but it's also worth noting that while everyone can use this system now, it's still the Ronin's system, and he will have *many* more interactions and synergies with it than the other classes will. Also he's near on the horizon, so stay tuned for that!
[b]
Ki/technique rework:[/b]
-All classes now have access to Ki. Ki is a little complicated, but the short version is that you can have between 0-3 ki levels, it grows when you melee attack, and it decays when out of combat. It takes quite a bit of combat to reach max ki, so it's not useful for everyone.
-Weapon techniques now either cost Ki or generate it. A rare few are more or less the same.
-Weapon techniques are now balanced according to ki cost, with most becoming more powerful or shifting to a ki-generation role. Their fatigue costs have gone down across the board.
-Added a new polearm technique, Impale. It pretty much just does what you think it does, but polearms only had 3 techs, so it was added to maintain parity. Most weapons follow the format of "generation technique, 1-cost technique, 2-cost technique, 3/all cost technique". 
-Having a weapon proficiency now grants you a free technique, which varies from weapon type to weapon type. Not only does this always give players one technique to use, but due to those techniques being removed from the scroll pool, finding more good techs should be easier as well.
-The shop algorithm now forces there to be some unlearned technique scrolls for weapons that you currently have equipped at the time of generation (I.E. leaving the boss floor). The more possible techniques there are, the higher the amount of forced spawns. You could try to manipulate this if you wish, although I'm not sure how useful it would be.
-PRECISION now affects ki generation rather than reducing technique costs. Other effects that reduce technique costs are still unchanged as of yet.

[b]Other gameplay:[/b]
-Exertion no longer ticks down when in safe zones. Baths will still restore it as normal. The reason for this is mostly due to being able to summon repeatedly in safe areas, this was an intentional behaviour, however people could summon a lot more monsters this way than anticipated by resting. 
-Boss levels now count as a safe zone until the fight is triggered.
-Broadspear's weight reduced from 15 to 12.
-You can now take a Scroll of Mastery at the start, although it's meant to be a silly option.
-Wind Slash can no longer sneak or ambush attack(it was a bit crazy with the new technique powerlevel)

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Updated the prayer beads description to make it more clear what they actually do.
-More typos fixed.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed the blood pool description (corruption value was wrong)
-Fixed a bug where being in/out of combat(for regen purposes) wasn't actually saving or loading
-Fixed a bug where shuten would accept divine sake multiple times
-Fixed a bug where thunder slash did no actual lightning damage
-Fixed a bug where enemy attacks were never deflecting off of the player's armor when they were supposed to

notes.title: Patch 0.6.05/hotfix
notes.content:
More like a hotfix that a patch. Or I guess you can call it a very fast an early patch due to an unexpected and somewhat critical error popping up right after I added a few things.

Gameplay:
-Changed the default event art slightly.
-Added artwork for:
--Massacre

QOL:

Bugfixes:

notes.title: 0.6.04 hotfix
notes.content: Fixed an issue where the help files couldn't be accessed.

notes.title: Patch 0.6.04: Mouse support and more!
notes.content:
Shadowed's next patch comes with mouse support! Any feedback related to it is appreciated, as it may still be a little rough around the edges.

Gameplay:
-Movement fatigue is now affected by current encumbrance, scaling to +/-50% depending on how close you are to the limit. The penalty for being over-encumbered has worsened slightly.
-Increasing fatigue via level up now grants +5 max carry weight(up from +2)

QOL:
-Updated some perk descriptions and help files for more clarity.
-Base attack damage displayed in charinfo should now reflect global damage multipliers.
-Confirm screen events(eg stairs) can now be progressed by just pressing enter.
-Added mouse support. There are very likely to be parts missing or bugs.
-Attempted to replace combat log with a "monsters are fighting somewhere" message when allies are engaged in combat far away from the player. It probably isn't working for every single action a distant monster can do right now, but it should help.
--Most HUD elements now have tooltips
--Targeting can be done with the mouse
--Looking around can be done with the mouse
--Chargen can be navigated with the mouse. Makes picking items much easier!
--Character screen has mouse navigation, and now many tooltips. The actual display and layout have been reworked and improved somewhat.
--Miscellaneous menus now have mouse support also.

Bugfixes:
-Fixed a bug where it was possible to charm sleeping monsters.
-Fixed a bug where running in the garden levels did not stop next to passageways.
-Fixed a bug where your inventory would permanently display traps only when cancelling out of set trap command.
-Fixed a bug where values such as dodge could be displayed with decimals
-Fixed a bug where the old man couldn't tell if you actually already had sake/elixir or not

notes.title: 0.6.03 Hotfix
notes.content:
-Added the ability to move diagonally with the regular arrow keys by holding ALT
-Changed F1 key's old function to F2.
-You can now view the help menu by pressing F1.

notes.title: Patch 0.6.03
notes.content:
Even more bugfixes and QOL changes, as well as very minor gameplay updates.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
-Passageway tiles now reduce your vision radius to 1 instead of 0
-Reduced the sight range of all enemies by 1 tile in order to help wih stealth. Sight range now also varies from monster to monster, though most just have the default, and the ranges do not display in the info window as of yet.
-Adjusted item spawn rates in forest slightly (less food, more pills now)

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
-Fixed a bug where quickstepping onto a grass tile would remove your hide state
-Fixed a visual bug where the perk table was duplicating in certain circumstances
-Fixed a crash when picking equipment in certain event options
-Fixed a bug where failing a ranged attack due to charm could cause a softlock
-Fixed an issue with traps always being visible

[b]QOL:[/b]
-Changed "alerted" exp modifier to "disturbed", to make it more clear that it doesn't trigger when a monster is aggroed
-Improved floor tile descriptions
-Added a border to the map for clarity
-Spirit poison now displays as "s.poison" instead of "spoison"
-Changed the color of the damage taken/damage dealt messages
-Added a feature that lets you see item descriptions while in shop
-Added a light background to items that are hard to see on colored map floors
-Fixed a bug where sleeping monsters could investigate with allies(tag along)
-Sped up the scrolling in the help window
-Minor typo fixes
-Fixed the number entry window being too small and in the wrong spot

notes.title: Patch 0.6.02
notes.content:
Shadowed's first patch comes with many QOL updates and bugfixes.
[b]
Full changelog:[/b]

-Reworked the monster info system to require less scrolling. Probably still needs more work, but it's improved.
-Fixed issue with audio options adjusting the volume poorly

-Added a message when taking damage from status effects
